sources.title: Public Holidays Act (Chapter 174), as at 31 December 2023 (revised and consolidated by the Law Reform Commission of Uganda; Laws.Africa for ULII)
sources.said: 2. (1) The days specified in Schedule 2 to this Act are declared to be public holidays, which, subject to this Act, shall in every year be kept and observed as public holidays throughout Uganda. (2) In addition ... the President may declare any other day to be a public holiday, and may limit the observation of any such public holiday to any area or place in Uganda. ... Schedule 2: Archbishop Janan Luwum Day - 16th February; Birth of Prophet Muhammed Day; Boxing Day - 26th December; Christmas Day - 25th December; Easter Monday; Good Friday; Idd Adhua; Idd el-Fitr Day; Idd-ul-Zuho Day; Independence Day - 9th October; Labour Day - 1st May; Martyrs’ Day - 3rd June; National Heroes Day - 9th June; New Year’s Day - 1st January; Women’s Day - 8th March. (Idd Adhua and Idd-ul-Zuho are both names of the feast of sacrifice, kept once.)
sources.note: Until 2026-11-03 this consolidation was cited as primary; it is a legal information institute's copy of the law, so secondary since the ruling of 2026-11-03 (Laws.Africa's consolidated text of the Uganda Law Reform Commission's Revised Edition, 2023), so it was relabelled, naming the Commission's Laws of Uganda, and the fact is held as secondary. Tried that day for the state's own text: Laws.Africa's gazette scan of the 1965 Act (none: 404), the Commission's Laws of Uganda (a script-drawn app whose documents sit behind its own API), a web search for a .go.ug copy (none found; two Ugandan missions' holiday pages answered 404), and Common Crawl (its index answered 403 every time).
